title: Find the Minimum Amount of Time to Brew Potions
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<long long> f: n entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vectors skill, mana
approach: Track each wizard's earliest free time f[i] after the last potion. For each new potion with mana x, do a forward pass computing the actual start time now = max(now + skill[i-1]*x, f[i]), giving completion f[n-1] = now + skill[n-1]*x; then back-propagate f[i] = f[i+1] - skill[i+1]*x so every wizard's timeline is consistent with this potion's actual schedule. This is O(n·m) = 25M operations for n,m ≤ 5000, and correctness follows because each wizard starts a potion exactly when it arrives, no earlier than their free time.
hints:
Potion j+1 cannot simply start when potion j leaves wizard 0 - wizard 3 might still be busy. If you knew exactly when each wizard finished the previous potion, what determines the earliest moment the new potion can pass through wizard i?
(Example 1 shows potion 1 waiting until t = 52 even though wizard 0 was free at t = 60... or was it earlier?)

Keep an array f[] of each wizard's free time. For mana = 1 with skill = [1,1,1]: forward pass gives starts 0→1→2, end = 3; then walk backwards setting f[1] = 3−1 = 2, f[0] = 2−1 = 1, so the next potion starts at 1 and finishes at 4.

**Overflow** - with n = m = 5000 and all values 5000, the answer is 5000·5000·(5000·5000) = 6.25×10^14, far past 2^31−1.
`Input: skill = [5000]*5000, mana = [5000]*5000` → `Expected: 625000000000000`
⚠️ Bug: accumulating times in int → overflow, returns a garbage/wrapped value instead of 625000000000000.

**Single wizard** - no passing between wizards, answer is just the sum of skill[0]*mana[j].
`Input: skill = [2], mana = [3,4]` → `Expected: 14`
⚠️ Bug: a loop written for i in 1..n-1 that also runs when n = 1 reads skill[0] twice → returns 20 instead of 14.

**Wizard 3 still busy** - the forward pass must take the max with the wizard's free time, not just accumulate.
`Input: skill = [1,5], mana = [2,2]` → `Expected: 22`
⚠️ Bug: computing now = now + skill[i-1]*x without max(now, f[i]) → returns 14 instead of 22.

**All equal values** - every potion waits exactly one wizard-step; check the back-propagation keeps f strictly consistent.
`Input: skill = [1,1], mana = [2,2]` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: back-propagating f[i] = f[i+1] - skill[i]*x (wrong index) → f[0] = 4, next potion ends at 8 instead of 6.

followUps.q: Return the completion time of every potion instead of only the last one.
followUps.a: Record f[n-1] after each potion's forward+backward pass into a result vector. Same O(n·m) time, space becomes O(n + m).

followUps.q: Mana values arrive as a stream (you cannot store all m potions).
followUps.a: The algorithm already processes potions one at a time and only needs the f[] array, so streaming works unchanged: O(n) extra space, O(n) per potion, O(n·m) total.

followUps.q: Each wizard needs a fixed cooldown c[i] before starting a new potion - how does the solution change?
followUps.a: In the forward pass use now = max(now + skill[i-1]*x, f[i] + c[i]) and back-propagate f[i] = f[i+1] - skill[i+1]*x as before; time stays O(n·m), space O(n).
